OnPlay.rationale: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04 (file re-shrunk since last audit; only line numbers moved, logic unchanged). The amount and target match, but the VERB differs: C# calls `PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["StrengthPower"].BaseValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (Inflame.cs:32) while the sim calls `StrengthCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, self._strength, card=self)` (inflame.py:34), which runs `hooks.modify_strength_given` before `PowerCmd.apply(StrengthPower)` (cmds.py:1155-1167, was `:349-361`). Recorded as a deliberate divergence rather than a gap and carrying the same verdict as card/fight_me's guard (rule 3): the sim's `StrengthCmd` is a documented re-architecture of C#'s `Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven` / `...Received` chain, which `PowerCmd.Apply` runs anyway (PowerCmd.cs:120-125), so the observable Strength gained is the same. It becomes a gap if a ported `modify_strength_given` listener ever diverges from the general power-amount modifiers. Presentation, folded in: NPowerUpVfx (31).
